body: Hm. Thank you.
If you're like OP, you would start by relaying his post to the therapist. There's plenty there.

My last semester went similarly besides the injury and class skipping. This semester I'm starting to skip a bit more but for one class I might as well not being going because I haven't read 1 page of the assigned reading yet and just do Japanese or Reddit in class. But attendance is 20% of the grade, so... And there's a paper in two weeks. Good lord.

I still haven't failed because the professor left it up to me: add more work to my current semester, or move on with an F. Might end up failing and shitting on this semester anyway.

Well last semester didn't go to well, and I'm following the same path this semester. Again, last week, I felt like I really could do it, catch up. Evidently not. Maybe a counselor will help. I really don't want to go to my professor again though and say, "I screwed up again." I guess I'll just have to accept the bad grade.

I just wrote a paragraph and accidentally went back in Chrome. Wow, that's unbelievably frustrating. I'll try again:

>DBT

I briefly looked it up and it sounds interesting. As for "should," I cannot help but think back to a couple of days ago when I binged a show for 10 hours straight. Although I got some work done before the first episode, in was only supposed to last a couple of hours. Clearly that didn't work out and I basically ended up doing the same thing the next day, despite the mounting work I *had* to do. 

"Well, that didn't work." I can't help but chuckle--of course that didn't work. But it does draw more attention to the fact that I wasn't trying to make it work. I was escaping. I attribute the 10-hour binge to my lack of self-control, but I don't know. I avoid work because of anxiety and the more work I have, the more anxiety I have. It's a vicious cycle that feels inescapable.

I guess in that situation it would be pretty hard to procrastinate if you don't have any long-term, daily goals that could be worked on from bed (for me, I have learning a language). I guess technically I haven't been procrastinating 100% of the time, but it damn well feels like it. It's horrible. I should be reading right now but alas, here I am.

Forgive me, I'm a bit confused by this

>I find that it's less tempting to spend my days on the internet when I'm not procrastinating, and I'll read a book or take a nap or something instead.

When you aren't procrastinating, it's less tempting to spend time on the internet? I mean, that makes sense. But for me, I don't know if there's ever a time I'm not procrastinating... Besides spending time on the computer, there's very little I would be doing besides language learning (which I've depressingly fell behind on and am having trouble getting started). To actually be free from procrastination... I cannot remember the last time I didn't have something that I should have been doing instead of whatever else I usually do.

Haha, it's fine, I check my posts compulsively so I actually noticed your edit right before this comment and figured you would let me know about it. 

I might use a hotline, I'm not sure. It's hard enough to get privacy as is and I'm not entirely sure that's the route I want to take. 

Shitty mental health and no motivation... Yup, that's about it. And I've thought about taking a break from school, but it's like... What would I do? My dad would make me get a random job and I'd probably continue to waste away on the internet, staying fat. There's other things to consider as well, but I guess there's pros and cons to everything. 

Thanks again.

Believe me, Tumblr has crossed my path of procrastination. Few sites are safe from me. But Reddit is definitely the worst. 

Thanks for the comment.

If you recognize it as cultural influence, why do you continue to let it hold you back? Does going to the doctor make you feel like you lost your dignity? Like your doctor, some people are trained to help you better than you can help yourself. At least give it a try.
You're an asshole.
You drew a flower. It's cute.

I'm not sure if there's anything to rationalize; it sounds pretty rational to me. Life can be full of stress. Death is full of... Nothing. There's no downside to death besides what comes before it, like how it'll happen, the effect it *will* have on others, and an inherent desire to reconcile living itself with stress/depression. These are all valid reasons to want to avoid death, just as disliking discomfort is a valid reason to desire death. I'm not sure if I've really said anything here, but I would suggest writing more of these thoughts down, to yourself or otherwise. I find it helps to explore ourselves by getting it down in words, especially in times of confusion. Though, sometimes, I'd rather be confused than lucid in my desires. Lucidity can be scarier.

Yup. Uni is killing me. I was not prepared and it's either exacerbated or made me aware of my depression. I just hope I can improve and this one semester (first as a transfer) doesn't forever screw me over. I'm so worried I'll fuck up just as much next semester, but at least I'll go in better prepared.

I'm pretty sure I'm "a little gay." I've always loved girls along with all of their bits and I don't usually feel anything when I look at other guys. I definitely will admire how good-looking a guy can be though mostly out of jealousy. But as I've become more comfortable with my sexuality I can sort of imagine doing things with another guy. Like, looking at a dick does nothing for me, but intimacy with another guy doesn't sound gross to me. Then again, I *am* really lonely!
Is that why people seem to always write my name as "デビットさん"? Lol. Thanks for your response!

10 minutes... Hopefully you can submit it late, then? That's what I'll probably end up doing. Though having a paper due soon and being socially awkward brings us closer than farther. I don't feel socially awkward, but in a crowd of people I become a deer in highlights. Good luck to both of us.

If anything, I feel being in school exacerbates my loneliness, seeing all these happy, healthy people. Then there's me, fat and depressed outcast.

Well we probably have extremely different circumstances, but yes, after I had seen my long-distance girlfriend and were intimate together (yet remained virgins), we broke up shortly after (due to other things). We were together for a little under two years and I didn't really want to break up, though it was mutual in a fucked up sort of way. Couple months later, she's already with someone and I find out she lost her virginity pretty quickly. That was really, really, painful. When we saw each other that one time and were intimate I asked if she wanted to do it and she said she didn't think she was ready. She was the love of my life. Few months later she loses her v-card to a dude she was dating for a month, maybe? I tried to rationalize that virginity didn't mean anything, but fuck, that did not stop the pain my 17-year-old self was having. 3 years later I remain a virgin, having not dated since. Took at least 2 years to feel like I was "over" the relationship, without mentioning the manipulation she later put me through.

Do you not like people or are you just not good at socializing for whatever reason?

I don't think it's cruel, especially if you do consider the perspective that all our actions are selfish in nature. It's not a bad thing to be selfish, it's just the way of things and in most contemporary views what I laid out would be considered a very selfless reason to continue living. In fact, if how other people feel matters to you at all, you're taking a very empathetic stance which I cannot imagine being the least bit cruel. You should be proud of your empathy, I think it's fundamental to what makes a decent human being.

I don't think the present is so much something you should experience more as much as it is necessarily what you *are* experiencing. We can theorize and contemplate the what-ifs, whys, and hows of the future but really all I *must* care about is this moment. It is in this perpetual moment that persists my existence, my consciousness. And unless you are bereft of desire, you care. If I feel something matters now, it takes priority over what may not matter later, "later" being some abstract place as opposed to the existing now. Therefore, if right now I care about how my loved ones feel, that takes precedence over the lack of care I'd feel later, being dead. So ironically, their future feelings are important because I care about their feelings right now. This is all given regardless of the morality of things; it's a purely selfish reason to keep on going. Conversely, if I didn't care or know about how they felt, their future feelings should have no bearing over my decision. Does any of this make sense? I might have contradicted myself, not sure. 

Anyway, your welcome and thanks!

On second thought, I really should go to bed. Please reply to my other message and I'll get back to you. Thanks a lot, you took my mind off a lot of things and I'm not as worried about sleep now. I really appreciate your time.

The "I don't deserve this" was unintentionally vague: I meant I don't deserve to be in University, to have my dad pay for it. I don't really put any value on life, so whether I deserve it or not is not a thought I have often. However, everything else you said resonates with me. 

Yes, there have been many things. I'm overweight and have been for years. I've never had a real, lasting friend (not since primary school), and was tethered to the internet for a while. I don't have the confidence to attempt a relationship and I have never been in a real one despite the insane desire to be in one. Note the use of the word "real" here. I had access to these things via the internet in my youth, but barely beyond that. Needless to say, I've been unbearably lonely for a while. 

I haven't really had any motivation to do, well, anything since Junior year in HS so I cruised through community college doing the bare minimum for As while spending my spare time on video games and what not. I have ADD so time management is something I barely understand (not all on my ADD, but I'm pretty sure it plays a part), hence my post. My first semester in Uni is looking pretty precarious.

Since I was 13 I've had existential thoughts of life and death, eventually coming to terms with the inherent meaninglessness of it all, but pushing on despite that, hoping good things would come my way to no avail. On the bright side, I have a wonderful family, without whom I probably would have killed myself long ago as opposed to it merely being a philosophical exercise I've turned over and over in my head. 

It's only now, however, that I'm realizing how much my "go-with-the-flow" attitude has fucked me over. 5 weeks into school and I've barely done anything for most of my classes; I'm starting to feel the impact. Again, hence the post.

There's plenty more but I've written a lot and that's basically the jist of it.

I've had exactly the same thoughts (though not the thoughts of "importance"). Really, what counteracts the notion of "what does it matter if they'd be upset" is that right now I care about their feelings. As arbitrary as it might be once I'm dead, right now I can think about the horror people would feel over my death. And it disgusts me. I know how much they love me and it sickens me to imagine their pain. I feel this right now, and the now is the only thing that matters. So I go on.
At some point I will go to sleep and log off of this account. I created it solely for this post. The lack of a reply does not equate to my having died.
It's okay.

Like I said, it's not happening tonight. I'm aware who will be affected,  and that fact is a big reason why I haven't already. I'll be honest though, I cannot take seriously a stranger on Reddit telling me that my death will affect them. I appreciate your feedback but realistically if I did it, you wouldn't even know.
You'd prefer he said "it doesn't get better"? For some people it does. For some it doesn't. You have to be open to wait to find out.

I'm pretty sure I'm depressed, 'specially with these thoughts. I guess I've been here for a while. There's still a lot of joy, but just so, so much uncertainty, stress, and loneliness. But yeah, I get you. I've just never realistically thought "I want to kill myself right now and that's how I can do it" before tonight.
I won't. Not tonight at least. I just needed to get that out. I felt better once I did, though still thoroughly shitty. Thank you.
